reinforcement learning: Learning by trial and error. An agent tries actions, gets rewards, and gradually works out which actions lead to more reward. Nobody shows it the right answer.
agent: The one doing the acting. In reinforcement learning it is the learner: it looks at its situation, picks an action and collects the reward.
state (in reinforcement learning): The situation an agent is in right now, as far as it can tell. In the maze it is the cell the creature is standing on.
action: One of the things an agent can choose to do. In the maze there are four: up, right, down and left.
reward: The number an agent gets back right after an action: points gained or lost. In reinforcement learning it is the only feedback there is.
episode: One complete attempt in reinforcement learning, from the starting position until the goal is reached or time runs out.
policy: An agent’s rule for which action to take in every state. In the maze it is the map of arrows.
Q-learning: A reinforcement learning method that keeps a value for every action in every state and corrects one value after each move, using the reward and the best value of the state it landed in.
Q-value: An agent’s current estimate of the total reward that one action, taken from one state, will lead to in the end.
Q-table: The table a Q-learning agent fills in: one Q-value for every action in every state.
exploration: Trying an action you are not sure about, to find out what happens.
exploitation: Taking the action you currently believe is best, instead of trying something new.
discount factor: A number between 0 and 1, written γ, that says how much a reward one step in the future is worth compared with the same reward right now.
deep Q-network: A neural network that does the job of a Q-table: the state goes in and an estimated value for each action comes out. Often shortened to DQN.
self-play: Training a game-playing agent by having it play against copies of itself.
reward hacking: When an agent finds a way to collect lots of reward that is not what its designers meant.
